# Custom resource definitions

The custom resource definitions of the `gentianos.io` API group, with every field of their `spec` and `status`. Paths are dotted from the object root; `[]` marks the items of a list and `{}` the values of a map. `apiVersion`, `kind` and `metadata` are the standard object fields and are not listed.

| Kind | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [App](#1-app) | Namespaced |  |
| [AppGrant](#2-appgrant) | Namespaced | AppGrant is a tenant-scoped authorization grant — a subset of what the ComponentProfile declares. |
| [AppPackage](#3-apppackage) | Cluster | AppPackage is a named addon preset for a family. |
| [BackupPolicy](#4-backuppolicy) | Cluster | BackupPolicy is where a tenant's bundles go, how often, and how long they are kept. |
| [Branding](#5-branding) | Cluster | Branding is the brand every page on the cluster shows: the concierge, the identity provider's screens, the desktop and the consoles. |
| [BundleSource](#6-bundlesource) | Cluster | BundleSource is a place outside the cluster bundles are imported from, declared by the cluster's administrator. |
| [Component](#7-component) | Namespaced | Component is an installed instance of a ComponentProfile. |
| [ComponentProfile](#8-componentprofile) | Cluster | ComponentProfile is a catalog entry for a system service, an app or an agent. |
| [CredentialRequirement](#9-credentialrequirement) | Cluster | CredentialRequirement declares a secret that must be supplied from outside the cluster: a registry token, a DNS provider key, an SMTP relay password. |
| [Customization](#10-customization) | Namespaced | Customization is a tracked, owned, dated deviation from an app as shipped. |
| [IntegrationBinding](#11-integrationbinding) | Namespaced | IntegrationBinding is the Schema for the integrationbindings API. |
| [MailboxRemoval](#12-mailboxremoval) | Cluster | MailboxRemoval records what whoever removed a person decided about that person's mailbox, and what became of it. |
| [OIDCPackCatalog](#13-oidcpackcatalog) | Cluster | OIDCPackCatalog is a cluster-scoped catalog of OIDC packs for tenant apps. |
| [PlatformSecurityPolicy](#14-platformsecuritypolicy) | Cluster | PlatformSecurityPolicy is the cluster singleton where platform administrators approve MAC waivers and other cluster-wide security posture settings. |
| [ProfileBuild](#15-profilebuild) | Cluster | ProfileBuild is one build of a profile, as a catalog published it: the bundle at one digest, kept on the cluster for as long as a tenant runs it. |
| [ResourcePlan](#16-resourceplan) | Cluster | ResourcePlan is a named preset of tenant resource limits. |
| [Tenant](#17-tenant) | Cluster | Tenant is the Schema for the tenants API. |
| [TenantBackupPolicy](#18-tenantbackuppolicy) | Namespaced | TenantBackupPolicy overrides the cluster backup policy for one tenant. |
| [TenantDomain](#19-tenantdomain) | Cluster | TenantDomain moves the tenant it is named after to spec.domain. |
| [TenantExport](#20-tenantexport) | Namespaced | TenantExport captures one tenant's data into an encrypted bundle. |
| [TenantExportSchedule](#21-tenantexportschedule) | Namespaced | TenantExportSchedule creates TenantExports on a cron schedule. |
| [TenantRestore](#22-tenantrestore) | Namespaced | TenantRestore restores a tenant's data from a bundle. |
| [XTenant](#23-xtenant) | Cluster |  |

AppGrant is a tenant-scoped authorization grant — a subset of what the ComponentProfile declares.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |

| `spec` | object |  | AppGrantSpec defines tenant-approved integration permissions for one installed app. |
| `spec.allowConsumers` | []object |  | `AllowConsumers` controls which other installed apps may invoke this app's provides contracts. |
| `spec.allowConsumers[].app` | string | yes | `App` is the consumer ComponentProfile name. |
| `spec.allowConsumers[].contract` | string | yes | `Contract` matches ComponentProfile.spec.provides[].name. |
| `spec.allowConsumers[].scope` | []string | yes | `Scope` lists approved capability strings for the consumer. |
| `spec.app` | string | yes | `App` is the installed ComponentProfile name (matches Tenant.spec.apps[].profile). |
| `spec.consume` | []object |  | `Consume` lists contract capabilities this app may use from providers in the tenant. |
| `spec.consume[].contract` | string | yes | `Contract` matches IntegrationBinding.spec.contract. |
| `spec.consume[].granted` | []string | yes | `Granted` lists approved capability strings (subset of the binding declaration). |
| `status` | object |  | AppGrantStatus holds observed grant state. |
| `status.conditions` | []object |  | `Conditions` provide detailed status. |
| `status.conditions[].lastTransitionTime` | string (date-time) | yes | `lastTransitionTime` is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. |
| `status.conditions[].message` | string | yes | `message` is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. |
| `status.conditions[].observedGeneration` | integer (int64) |  | `observedGeneration` represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. |
| `status.conditions[].reason` | string | yes | `reason` contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition. |
| `status.conditions[].status` | string | yes | `status` of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown. |
| `status.conditions[].type` | string | yes | `type` of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase. |
| `status.observedGeneration` | integer (int64) |  | `ObservedGeneration` is the last reconciled spec generation. |
| `status.phase` | string |  | `Phase` summarizes OpenFGA tuple sync. |
| `status.tupleCount` | integer |  | `TupleCount` is the number of OpenFGA tuples managed for this grant. |

## 4. BackupPolicy

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Group | `gentianos.io` |
| Version | `v1alpha1` |
| Scope | Cluster |
| Plural | `backuppolicies` |
| Short names | `bkpol` |

BackupPolicy is where a tenant's bundles go, how often, and how long they are kept. Cluster-scoped for both scopes, as CredentialRequirement is: the console mediates access by spec.tenant, and the credential itself is governed by the OpenBao policy its scope selects. The name is not free. Every reader of a policy fetches it by name — the cluster's as "default", a tenant's as the tenant's own name — so a policy whose name does not match its scope is never read by anything. That failed silently: the policy reported Accepted, published an effective destination, and bundles went to the platform's own storage as though it had never been written. The two rules below make that object unadmittable rather than merely ineffective.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec` | object |  | BackupPolicySpec is one backup arrangement: the cluster's default, or one tenant's override of it. |
| `spec.allowTenantOverride` | boolean |  | `AllowTenantOverride` lets tenants state policies of their own. |
| `spec.destination` | object |  | `Destination` is where bundles are written. |
| `spec.destination.addressingStyle` | string |  | `AddressingStyle` is how a bucket is named in a request to Endpoint: path (https://host/bucket/key, the default when empty) or virtualHost… |
| `spec.destination.bucket` | string |  | `Bucket` holds the bundles. |
| `spec.destination.endpoint` | string |  | `Endpoint` is the S3 API URL, e.g. https://sos-ch-gva-2.exo.io or https://s3.example.org:9000. |
| `spec.destination.region` | string |  | `Region`, for providers that require one — Exoscale SOS and AWS do, the platform's own store does not. |
| `spec.encryption` | object |  | `Encryption` names the keys bundles are encrypted to. |
| `spec.encryption.recipients` | []string |  | `Recipients` are age public keys (age1…) to encrypt to. |
| `spec.retention` | object |  | `Retention` decides which bundles survive. |
| `spec.retention.keepDaily` | integer (int32) |  | `KeepDaily`, KeepWeekly, KeepMonthly and KeepYearly each retain the most recent export within that many distinct periods. |
| `spec.retention.keepLast` | integer (int32) |  | `KeepLast` retains this many most recent finished exports regardless of age. |
| `spec.retention.keepMonthly` | integer (int32) |  |  |
| `spec.retention.keepWeekly` | integer (int32) |  |  |
| `spec.retention.keepYearly` | integer (int32) |  |  |
| `spec.schedule` | string |  | `Schedule` is a five-field cron expression, in UTC. |
| `spec.scope` | string | yes | `Scope` decides whether this is the cluster default or one tenant's override, and with it who may edit the policy and which OpenBao path its credential lives at. |
| `spec.suspendSchedule` | boolean |  | `SuspendSchedule` turns scheduled backups off, distinctly from inheriting. |
| `spec.tenant` | string |  | `Tenant` names the tenant a tenant-scoped policy belongs to. |
| `status` | object |  | BackupPolicyStatus reports what this policy resolved to and whether it can actually be used. |
| `status.conditions` | []object |  | `Conditions` carries Accepted: whether this policy is permitted and usable. |
| `status.conditions[].lastTransitionTime` | string (date-time) | yes | `lastTransitionTime` is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. |
| `status.conditions[].message` | string | yes | `message` is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. |
| `status.conditions[].observedGeneration` | integer (int64) |  | `observedGeneration` represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. |
| `status.conditions[].reason` | string | yes | `reason` contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition. |
| `status.conditions[].status` | string | yes | `status` of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown. |
| `status.conditions[].type` | string | yes | `type` of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase. |
| `status.credentialRequirement` | string |  | `CredentialRequirement` names the requirement carrying this destination's keys, and CredentialSatisfied reports whether it has been filled. |
| `status.credentialSatisfied` | boolean |  |  |
| `status.effectiveBucket` | string |  |  |
| `status.effectiveEndpoint` | string |  | `EffectiveEndpoint`, EffectiveBucket and EffectiveSchedule are the values in force after inheritance, published so an admin reads what applies rather than… |
| `status.effectiveRecipients` | []string |  | `EffectiveRecipients` are the age public keys in force, empty when the cluster's own key is used. |
| `status.effectiveSchedule` | string |  |  |
| `status.observedGeneration` | integer (int64) |  |  |

Branding is the brand every page on the cluster shows: the concierge, the identity provider's screens, the desktop and the consoles. One per cluster, named "default"; without it they show the platform's own.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec` | object |  | BrandingSpec is the cluster's brand. |
| `spec.identity` | object |  | `Identity` is the product's name and icons. |
| `spec.identity.description` | string |  | `Description` is the installed app's description. |
| `spec.identity.icons` | []object |  | `Icons` are the logo and favicon, as a manifest's icons: the first whose purpose includes "any" is the logo on the pages. |
| `spec.identity.icons[].purpose` | string |  | `Purpose`, as the manifest says it: any, maskable, monochrome. |
| `spec.identity.icons[].sizes` | string |  | `Sizes`, as the manifest says them: "any", or "192x192 512x512". |
| `spec.identity.icons[].src` | string | yes | `Src` is an https URL, or the image itself as a data URL. |
| `spec.identity.icons[].type` | string |  | `Type` is the image's media type: one of those a data URL may carry. |
| `spec.identity.name` | string |  | `Name` is the product's name, on sign-in cards, page titles and the sender of the identity provider's mail. |
| `spec.identity.shortName` | string |  | `ShortName` is where Name does not fit: an installed app's label. |
| `spec.tokens` | object (free-form) |  | `Tokens` is the brand's look: a design-token document in the W3C Design Tokens Community Group format (2025.10). |
| `status` | object |  | BrandingStatus says whether the brand is what the pages show. |
| `status.conditions` | []object |  | `Conditions`: Rendered is True once the pages' stylesheet is the brand's, False with the reason when the tokens cannot be rendered. |
| `status.conditions[].lastTransitionTime` | string (date-time) | yes | `lastTransitionTime` is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. |
| `status.conditions[].message` | string | yes | `message` is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. |
| `status.conditions[].observedGeneration` | integer (int64) |  | `observedGeneration` represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. |
| `status.conditions[].reason` | string | yes | `reason` contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition. |
| `status.conditions[].status` | string | yes | `status` of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown. |
| `status.conditions[].type` | string | yes | `type` of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase. |
| `status.observedGeneration` | integer (int64) |  | `ObservedGeneration` is the generation Rendered describes. |

## 6. BundleSource

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Group | `gentianos.io` |
| Version | `v1alpha1` |
| Scope | Cluster |

BundleSource is a place outside the cluster bundles are imported from, declared by the cluster's administrator. Cluster-scoped, and the cluster's: what it reaches is read to make a tenant, which is the cluster's administrator's to do. A tenant's own destination is its BackupPolicy's, and is read for its recovery as it is.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec` | object |  | BundleSourceSpec is S3 storage outside the cluster that bundles are read from: another cluster's destination, an old cluster's store, a provider's bucket a… |
| `spec.addressingStyle` | string |  | `AddressingStyle` is how a bucket is named in a request to Endpoint: path (the default when empty) or virtualHost. |
| `spec.bucket` | string | yes | `Bucket` holds the bundles. |
| `spec.description` | string |  | `Description` says what the storage is, for whoever picks a bundle from it. |
| `spec.endpoint` | string | yes | `Endpoint` is the S3 API URL, e.g. https://sos-ch-gva-2.exo.io. |
| `spec.prefix` | string |  | `Prefix` is where in the bucket the bundles are, each one a prefix of its own directly below it. |
| `spec.region` | string |  | `Region`, for a provider that requires one. |
| `status` | object |  | BundleSourceStatus reports whether the source can be read. |
| `status.conditions` | []object |  | `Conditions` carries Ready: whether bundles can be read from here. |
| `status.conditions[].lastTransitionTime` | string (date-time) | yes | `lastTransitionTime` is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. |
| `status.conditions[].message` | string | yes | `message` is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. |
| `status.conditions[].observedGeneration` | integer (int64) |  | `observedGeneration` represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. |
| `status.conditions[].reason` | string | yes | `reason` contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition. |
| `status.conditions[].status` | string | yes | `status` of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown. |
| `status.conditions[].type` | string | yes | `type` of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase. |
| `status.credentialRequirement` | string |  | `CredentialRequirement` names the requirement carrying the keys, and CredentialSatisfied reports whether it has been filled. |
| `status.credentialSatisfied` | boolean |  |  |
| `status.observedGeneration` | integer (int64) |  |  |

## 8. ComponentProfile

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Group | `gentianos.io` |
| Version | `v1alpha1` |
| Scope | Cluster |
| Plural | `componentprofiles` |
| Short names | `cprof` |

ComponentProfile is a catalog entry for a system service, an app or an agent. The cluster holds only the profiles something installed refers to.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec` | object |  | ComponentProfileSpec is one catalog entry: what a component is, what it needs from the platform, and what it may expose. |
| `spec.adapter` | object |  | `Adapter` is what an adapter adapts and the reviewed list of its tools. |
| `spec.adapter.adapts` | object |  | `Adapts` names the app whose interface this adapter uses: the app's ComponentProfile, which must be installed in the same tenant. |
| `spec.adapter.adapts.profile` | string | yes | `Profile` is the ComponentProfile of the app. |
| `spec.adapter.adapts.versions` | []string |  | `Versions` are the catalog versions of the app this adapter was reviewed against. |
| `spec.adapter.speaksAs` | string | yes | `SpeaksAs` is how a call reaches the app as the person on whose behalf it is made, in the order of preference the platform has: a short token for this app from… |
| `spec.adapter.tools` | []object | yes | `Tools` are the operations this adapter offers, each at a version. |
| `spec.adapter.tools[].class` | string |  | `Class` is whether the tool reads, changes, or changes irreversibly. |
| `spec.adapter.tools[].description` | map[string]string | yes | `Description` is the tool in plain words, by language (en, de, ...). |
| `spec.adapter.tools[].identifiers` | []string |  | `Identifiers` are the fields of the answer that the app made up, such as the number of a new task, by their JSON pointer into the answer. |
| `spec.adapter.tools[].input` | object (free-form) |  | `Input` is the JSON Schema of the tool's arguments. |
| `spec.adapter.tools[].name` | string | yes | `Name` of the tool, for example create-task. |
| `spec.adapter.tools[].output` | object (free-form) |  | `Output` is the JSON Schema of the tool's answer. |

## 9. CredentialRequirement

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Group | `gentianos.io` |
| Version | `v1alpha1` |
| Scope | Cluster |
| Plural | `credentialrequirements` |
| Short names | `credreq` |

CredentialRequirement declares a secret that must be supplied from outside the cluster: a registry token, a DNS provider key, an SMTP relay password. It is catalog data, not a provisioning API — a schema, a target path in OpenBao, and a validation hint. It is deliberately a plain CRD rather than a Crossplane XRD. It composes nothing: an XRD requires a Composition producing managed resources, and there are none to produce. It sits beside ComponentProfile as catalog. There is no controller. Each requirement emits an ExternalSecret, and ESO's sync status IS the satisfaction probe — path absent in OpenBao gives SecretSyncedError, path present gives Ready. That keeps satisfaction a Kubernetes condition (so Compositions can gate on it) and means no bespoke component has to hold an OpenBao token in order to poll. Naming: these are "credential requirements" or "credential inputs", never "external secrets". ESO's ExternalSecret is a reference to a secret stored externally, which is nearly the opposite of a secret that must be supplied from outside.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec` | object |  | CredentialRequirementSpec describes one credential an operator must supply. |
| `spec.consumedBy` | []object |  | `ConsumedBy` documents which resources depend on this credential. |
| `spec.consumedBy[].kind` | string | yes | `Kind` of the consuming resource, e.g. XRepository. |
| `spec.consumedBy[].name` | string | yes | `Name` of the consuming resource. |
| `spec.description` | string |  | `Description` explains what the credential is for and where to obtain it. |
| `spec.displayName` | string | yes | `DisplayName` is the label a form renders for this requirement. |
| `spec.fields` | []object | yes | `Fields` enumerates the keys stored at VaultPath. |
| `spec.fields[].example` | string |  | `Example` is a non-secret illustration of the expected shape. |
| `spec.fields[].format` | string |  | `Format` hints at how a form should render and check the field. |
| `spec.fields[].key` | string | yes | `Key` is the field name within the OpenBao secret. |
| `spec.fields[].minLength` | integer |  | `MinLength` enforces a minimum, declared once here rather than hardcoded at each site that checks it. |
| `spec.fields[].secret` | boolean |  | `Secret` marks a field whose value must never be displayed or logged. |
| `spec.optional` | boolean |  | `Optional` marks an unsatisfied requirement as an informational gap rather than an error. |
| `spec.phase` | string | yes | `Phase` decides whether an unsatisfied requirement blocks installation. |
| `spec.scope` | string | yes | `Scope` determines which OpenBao policy governs the write and who may see the requirement. |
| `spec.tenant` | string |  | `Tenant` names the tenant a tenant-scoped requirement belongs to. |
| `spec.validate` | object |  | `Validate` is the probe run BEFORE the value is written, so a bad paste becomes a red field at install time rather than a stalled provisioning job hours later. |
| `spec.validate.host` | string |  | `Host` is the endpoint probed, when the validator needs one that is not derivable from the fields themselves. |
| `spec.validate.type` | string | yes | `Type` keys the validator. |
| `spec.validate.url` | string |  | `URL` is the full endpoint probed, for validators that need a path. |
| `spec.vaultPath` | string | yes | `VaultPath` is the only coupling between this requirement and the storage layer. |

IntegrationBinding is the Schema for the integrationbindings API. IntegrationBinding is namespace-scoped — it lives in the tenant's namespace and is auto-generated by the orchestrator when both the provider and consumer apps are present in a tenant's app list and their profiles declare compatible integration contracts. The binding provisions shared credentials in OpenBao and wires the authentication method between provider and consumer.

## 12. MailboxRemoval

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Group | `gentianos.io` |

| Scope | Cluster |
| Plural | `mailboxremovals` |
| Short names | `mbxr` |

MailboxRemoval records what whoever removed a person decided about that person's mailbox, and what became of it. The registrar writes it, when a person is removed from a tenant that keeps mailboxes on the cluster's own mail server; the operator carries it out, by a Job beside the mail server's volume, and reports here. For as long as the mailbox is archived this is also the record an administrator reads the archive from, and where its deletion is asked for.

| `spec.deleteArchive.name` | string |  | `Name` is how the person is shown: their address or name at the time. |

| `spec.deleteArchive.subject` | string | yes | `Subject` is the person's id at the identity provider. |
| `spec.mailbox` | string | yes | `Mailbox` is the choice: archive or delete. |
| `spec.requestedBy` | object | yes | `RequestedBy` is who removed the person and made the choice. |
| `spec.requestedBy.at` | string (date-time) |  | `At` is when they asked. |
| `spec.requestedBy.name` | string |  | `Name` is how the person is shown: their address or name at the time. |
| `spec.requestedBy.requestID` | string |  | `RequestID` joins this to the registrar's record of the authority and to the identity provider's own event. |
| `spec.requestedBy.subject` | string | yes | `Subject` is the person's id at the identity provider. |
| `spec.restored` | object |  | `Restored` says this record was not written at a removal: a restore wrote it, for an archived mailbox it put back from a backup, so that the archive is listed… |
| `spec.restored.address` | string |  | `Address` is the address the removed person received at, in the domain of the tenant restored into. |
| `spec.restored.archive` | string | yes | `Archive` is the archived mailbox's name in the domain's archive. |
| `spec.restored.archivedAt` | string (date-time) |  | `ArchivedAt` is when it was archived, where the bundle was taken; By who chose that, as they were shown there. |
| `spec.restored.by` | string |  |  |
| `spec.restored.domain` | string |  | `Domain` is the mail domain whose archive it is in. |
| `spec.restored.messages` | integer (int64) |  |  |
| `spec.restored.sizeBytes` | integer (int64) |  |  |
| `spec.tenant` | string | yes | `Tenant` is the tenant the person was removed from. |

| `status.attempts` | integer (int32) |  | `Attempts` counts the Jobs that failed, and LastFailureAt is when the last one did: the next is started later each time. |
| `status.deletedAt` | string (date-time) |  |  |
| `status.domain` | string |  | `Domain` is the mail domain the mailbox was in. |
| `status.lastFailureAt` | string (date-time) |  |  |
| `status.message` | string |  | `Message` says, in a sentence, what happened or what is waited for. |
| `status.messages` | integer (int64) |  |  |
| `status.phase` | string |  | MailboxRemovalPhase is where a removed person's mailbox stands. |
| `status.refused` | boolean |  | `Refused` is set when the operator will not act on this record at all: the address is not one of the tenant's mailboxes, or still belongs to a person. |
| `status.signInGoneAt` | string (date-time) |  | `SignInGoneAt` is when the operator last saw that no mail password of the address is left with the mail server. |
| `status.sizeBytes` | integer (int64) |  | `SizeBytes` and Messages are what the mailbox held when it was archived or deleted. |

## 15. ProfileBuild

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Group | `gentianos.io` |
| Version | `v1alpha1` |
| Scope | Cluster |
| Plural | `profilebuilds` |
| Short names | `pb` |

ProfileBuild is one build of a profile, as a catalog published it: the bundle at one digest, kept on the cluster for as long as a tenant runs it. A ComponentProfile is one object per name for the whole cluster, and it is the newest build any tenant installed. A tenant pinned to another build runs it from here: the operator reads its profile out of the bundle this object carries, verified against the digest, and a profile's own Composition reads the same spec from profileSpec. So two tenants on two builds of one app share nothing, and a tenant moved back to a build it ran before finds it without fetching anything. Written by the director beside the profile, into the catalog directory of the deployments repository, and applied from there by Argo CD; the installer writes the same file for the profile it places. Nothing edits it: a build is its digest. The operator reads the bundle, holds it to the digest and to what a bundle may hold, and writes the profile's spec it found onto the status, which is what a profile's own Composition reads.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec` | object | yes | ProfileBuildSpec is the build. |
| `spec.bundle` | string | yes | `Bundle` is the published file, base64: the profile and its companions, the bytes that hash to Digest. |
| `spec.digest` | string | yes | `Digest` is the sha256 of the bundle, "sha256:\<hex>", as the catalog's index states it and as an install pins it. |
| `spec.origin` | string | yes | `Origin` is which catalog the bundle was fetched from, as the director records it on the profile (cluster/\<source> or tenant/\<t>/\<source>). |
| `spec.profile` | string | yes | `Profile` is the name of the ComponentProfile this is a build of: the app's identity across every build. |
| `status` | object |  | ProfileBuildStatus is what the operator found in the bundle. |
| `status.conditions` | []object |  | `Conditions`: Verified is True when the bundle is the digest it claims and holds what a bundle may; False names what was found. |
| `status.conditions[].lastTransitionTime` | string (date-time) | yes | `lastTransitionTime` is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. |
| `status.conditions[].message` | string | yes | `message` is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. |
| `status.conditions[].observedGeneration` | integer (int64) |  | `observedGeneration` represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. |

| `status.conditions[].type` | string | yes | `type` of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase. |

## 16. ResourcePlan

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Group | `gentianos.io` |
| Version | `v1alpha1` |
| Scope | Cluster |
| Plural | `resourceplans` |
| Short names | `rplan`, `rplans` |

ResourcePlan is a named preset of tenant resource limits. It is deliberately **not deployable**. Nothing reconciles a ResourcePlan and it owns no namespace, workload or quota of its own: it exists so that a tenant's ceiling is chosen from a catalog rather than typed. Selecting one writes its quantities into that tenant's `spec.quotas` — see docs/concepts/resource-plans.md. Why a catalog at all, when Tenant.spec.quotas already accepts any quantity: a quota that can be any number can be any number that was never sold. The plan is the unit the platform prices, meters and invoices, so the write path accepts a plan name and nothing else, and every tenant's ceiling is at all times one of a known, priced set. Free-form quantities remain available to whoever edits the deployments repository by hand, which is the cluster operator, which is the person entitled to make an unpriced choice. This mirrors the role AppPackage plays for addons: a curated preset that replaces a combinatorial choice with a named one, without becoming an artifact of its own.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec` | object |  | ResourcePlanSpec is the desired state of a ResourcePlan. |
| `spec.default` | boolean |  | `Default` marks the plan a tenant is assumed to be on when its quotas match no plan in the catalog and none has been selected. |
| `spec.description` | string |  | `Description` explains what the plan is for, in one or two sentences. |
| `spec.displayName` | string | yes | `DisplayName` is the name shown in the Admin Console (e.g. |
| `spec.productSku` | string |  | `ProductSku` identifies this plan to the commerce backend. |
| `spec.quotas` | object | yes | `Quotas` are the limits a tenant on this plan receives. |
| `spec.quotas.cpu` | int-or-string |  | `CPU` caps the sum of container CPU **limits** in the namespace. |
| `spec.quotas.maxApps` | integer (int32) |  | `MaxApps` is the maximum number of apps this tenant may install. |
| `spec.quotas.maxPods` | integer (int32) |  | `MaxPods` caps the number of pods in the tenant namespace (init Jobs + app workloads). |
| `spec.quotas.memory` | int-or-string |  | `Memory` caps the sum of container memory **limits** in the namespace. |
| `spec.quotas.requestsCpu` | int-or-string |  | `RequestsCPU` caps the sum of container CPU **requests** in the namespace. |
| `spec.quotas.requestsMemory` | int-or-string |  | `RequestsMemory` caps the sum of container memory **requests** in the namespace — reserved capacity, priced, as RequestsCPU is. |
| `spec.quotas.storage` | int-or-string |  | `Storage` is the total storage quota (PVCs + S3 buckets). |
| `spec.selfServiceDisabled` | boolean |  | `SelfServiceDisabled` withholds the plan from tenant administrators. |
| `spec.tier` | integer (int32) | yes | `Tier` orders plans from smallest to largest. |
| `status` | object |  | ResourcePlanStatus reports observed plan state. |
| `status.observedAt` | string (date-time) |  | `ObservedAt` is when TenantCount was last recomputed. |
| `status.tenantCount` | integer (int32) |  | `TenantCount` is the number of tenants whose quotas currently match this plan. |

## 17. Tenant

|---|---|
| Group | `gentianos.io` |

| Scope | Cluster |
| Plural | `tenants` |
| Short names | `tenant`, `tenants` |

Tenant is the Schema for the tenants API. Tenant is cluster-scoped and represents a customer organization. Creating a Tenant CR triggers the orchestrator's full provisioning pipeline: namespace creation, Keycloak realm, per-app databases/buckets/cache, and ArgoCD Application (or Crossplane App claim) CRs for each requested app.

## 19. TenantDomain

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Group | `gentianos.io` |
| Version | `v1alpha1` |
| Scope | Cluster |
| Plural | `tenantdomains` |
| Short names | `tdomain` |

TenantDomain moves the tenant it is named after to spec.domain. It is not a field on the Tenant: a custom domain is a separate decision with its own author, written beside the tenant's manifest by the director (PUT /v1/clusters/{c}/tenants/{t}/domain, can_configure) and shown in a console that offers it. The operator copies the domain to the Tenant's status.domain, which is what every consumer reads.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec` | object |  | TenantDomainSpec binds a tenant to a custom domain. |
| `spec.domain` | string | yes | `Domain` is where the tenant is served instead of \<tenant>.\<kernelDomain>: its zone, its hosts, its mail and its people's logins all move to it. |
